locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_cue_windows_round13.md · Measure and exact complementary determinant; separate signed totals
statement: The rank-two rooted CUE MGF equals e^(−H_N z_c) det A det(U* A^−1 U). For each tagged word with positive and negative totals P,Q≤n=N+1, the compressed inverse coefficient uses the oriented sum from Q to n−P; its constant/linear matrix is the polynomial in ell=n−P−Q and D=P−Q in the director note.
hypotheses: Global joint Haar-matrix/root-label derivative-square tilt with the deterministic root reinserted; formal coefficients at zero. The reversed interval contributes an oriented sum, including P=n or Q=n. No fixed-symbol asymptotic is invoked.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_cue_windows_round13.md · Joint quartic and exact finite-size surrogate
statement: At each fixed total degree r with rb≤1, the limiting mixed moments are the factorial-weighted coefficients of exp[H z_c+H(z_c²+z_s²)/4] [(1−d z_c)^4+2J3 z_c(1−d z_c)−3J2² z_s²], where H=log(b/a), d=b−a and J_j=(b^j−a^j)/j. The exact finite surrogate uses H_N, d_N, J_j,N and the n^−2 correction in the note.
hypotheses: Fixed 0<a<b<1; negative cosine/sine bands, one deterministic root, global rank-two tilt. Finite agreement through degree r holds for r K_N≤n=N+1. The arithmetic window remains rb<1/2 under RH; this result is intrinsic.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_cue_windows_round13.md · First new frequency chamber
statement: For (r−1)b≤1<rb, the first cosine raw-moment discrepancy from its formal continuation is −2^(1−r) I_r, where I_r=∫_{[a,b]^r, sum x_i>1}(2−4 sum x_i+2(sum x_i)^3) prod dx_i/x_i>0. The joint degree-r MGF difference is −[(z_c−i z_s)^r+(z_c+i z_s)^r] I_r/(2^r r!).
hypotheses: Same fixed rank-two model; only the first crossing is evaluated. The pure cosine sign is strict; mixed rays can vanish or change sign.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_cue_windows_round13.md · Independent exact finite and continuum checks
statement: For N=40, n=41 and modes 9,10,11 the exact fourth moment minus the formal surrogate is −3384187/302541624000. For band (0.22,0.28) an exact rational enclosure of the limiting fourth correction near −1.116093794622113479066e−5 has width <2.63e−27.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_cue_windows_round13.md · Every fixed integer tilt rank has an extrapolation barrier
statement: At fixed integer rank J≥1 the cosine-window coefficients for rb≤1 are those of exp[(J−1)H z+H z²/4] det B_J(z), with B_J the formal oriented Legendre matrix in the note, B_J(0)=I, and deg det B_J≤J².
hypotheses: Global root tilt |Z′|^(2(J−1)), ambient dimension N+J−1, one deterministic root, fixed positive band and fixed degree. Formal compound-Poisson notation computes polynomial coefficients.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_cue_windows_round13.md · Every fixed integer tilt rank has an extrapolation barrier
statement: For each integer J≥1 and fixed 0<a<b<1 the formal all-order cosine continuation has a positive real MGF zero and a finite negative square witness. For J≥3 the {0,2} principal minor at z=1/d has determinant −20(m3/d)², forcing a zero before 1/d. Centered finite Taylor approximants to exp(z* X/2) eventually have negative formal square expectation.
hypotheses: The polynomial-exponential signed inverse has Gaussian moment domination. The witness is at finite but potentially large degree in the formal sequence; no contradiction to the true finite window or novelty is claimed.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_cue_windows_round13.md · Every fixed integer tilt rank has an extrapolation barrier
statement: For (r−1)b≤1<rb the first cosine raw-moment discrepancy at fixed rank J has sign (−1)^(J+1). The pure-sign continuation A_J(t) has sign (−1)^J for t>1; rank three gives A_3(t)=−6t^5+12t³−9t+3 and a finite example with correction +9/160.
hypotheses: Intrinsic globally weighted rooted model. Christoffel–Darboux and Legendre parity apply to the reversed integration interval. This is a first crossing sign only.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_two_scale_round13.md · Statement with the quantifiers fixed
statement: For node increments bounded in pth moment by C min(h^a+epsilon_n,A_n h^b), the polygonal modulus satisfies ||omega(delta)||_p≤C1 [delta^((a′−1)/p)+lambda_n^(1/p) min(1,(delta/w_n)^((b′−1)/p))], where a′=min(a,p), b′=min(b,p), w_n=(epsilon_n/A_n)^(1/b), lambda_n=epsilon_n/w_n. The universal tightness criterion A_n epsilon_n^(b−1)→0 is sharp, with a single random spike giving failure otherwise.
hypotheses: Fixed p,a,b>1 and C>0, A_n≥1, 0<epsilon_n≤1 tending to zero, arbitrary deterministic finite grids, tight initial values for each family. A guarantee uniform across families needs uniformly tight initial values. Step transfer uses mesh→0, jumps→0, or exact composition and continuous clock comparison as specified. Necessity quantifies over grids and laws rather than one process.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_two_scale_round13.md · Direct exponents, arithmetic use and Lean boundary
statement: For 1<q≤min(a,b), the optimal scalar envelope constant is comparable to 1+A_n^(q/b) epsilon_n^(1−q/b). For a=b=2, A=L² and epsilon=L^−M, the sharp universal saving threshold is M>2 and the maximal common direct exponent is 2M/(M+2) as L→infinity.
hypotheses: All scalar distances 0<h≤1; realized distances in a particular grid can give stronger estimates. For M≤2 no uniform q>1 follows from the envelope. Polygonal interpolation caps the power at p.

statement: Lean declaration Observatory.twoScaleScalarBound proves X≤2 C u³ from X≤C(u⁴+v⁶), X v²≤C u⁴, 0≤u≤1, 0<v≤1 and C≥0. With h=u² and L=1/v this is the M=6 scalar step.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_hughes_rudnick_whole_round13.md · Statistic, literal hypotheses and repaired theorem
statement: The first m raw zero-statistic moments converge to the Gaussian moments of mean I=∫f and variance ∫min(|v|,1) fhat(v)² dv, provided I=0 or ∫w(u) log^m(2+|u|)du<infinity. For I≠0 that logarithmic moment is necessary for finiteness of the mth absolute moment at any fixed T>1,H>0.
hypotheses: No RH. Real even f with smooth compact Fourier transform in [−sigma,sigma], m sigma/2<a, H=T^a, 0<a≤1; evaluate the entire extension at complex ordinates. Nonnegative mass-one w with compact Fourier support. Finite moment window; the repair controls mixed gamma and polar terms additively.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_hughes_rudnick_whole_round13.md · Reconstruction of the valid argument
statement: The oscillatory prime statistic alone has the stated finite Gaussian moment window with the original nonnegative unit-mass bandlimited weights. Compact Fourier support eliminates unequal product frequencies and the leading equal-product terms give Wick pairings.
hypotheses: No RH and no logarithmic moment required for this oscillatory theorem. Same strict m sigma/2<a; the variance identification is needed only when m≥2. This theorem excludes the centering and polar contributions to the full statistic.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_pure_fourth_round13.md · Exact target and what is already covered
statement: For the cosine band W=Re D and 1/8<b<1/6, the difference between E_Y W⁴ and its formal fourth coefficient is (Re E_Y D⁴−m4_pure)/8+o(1), with m4_pure=4![z⁴] exp(H0 z)[(1−d z)^4+2m3 z(1−d z)+3m2² z²]. The mixed arms and a uniform sixth absolute moment are already covered.
hypotheses: RH, fixed 0<a<b, and the symmetric strict derivative-square tail. The 3+1 and 2+2 arms have longest length ≤Y^(3b)<sqrt(Y); the long pure arm is unresolved. Intrinsic CUE gives no arithmetic main term.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_pure_fourth_round13.md · One-sided continuous moments do not impose the half-power barrier
statement: The continuous shifted zeta product against one bounded-coefficient Dirichlet polynomial of length y≤T^theta, theta<1, has the explicit two-diagonal formula in the note with error O_epsilon(T^epsilon[(yT)^(1/2)+y^(1/4)T^(3/4)]), also with the logarithmic weight. The diagonal poles cancel.
hypotheses: Unconditional continuous-height integral, constant second arm and fixed microscopic shift radius. The direct asymmetric AFE proof does not estimate the discrete nonprincipal edge.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_pure_fourth_round13.md · A smooth contour formulation closes the saddle error
statement: A two-transition compact comparable-height cutoff of width H=T^kappa with kappa>(1+theta)/2, theta=4b, gives a reflected saddle error O(T/H²) per comparable term. The aggregated error is bounded by T^epsilon[T²y/H²+y+Ty/H]. Sharp zero-sum endpoints are recovered after differentiation with transition mass O(T^epsilon(H+Y^(2b))).
hypotheses: RH for the zero-sampling endpoint comparison, fixed microscopic shifts, theta<1 and kappa<1. The cutoff is shift-independent before differentiation. The result applies to the smooth saddle and does not recover the original hard arithmetic cutoff.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/uniform99_fixed_sequence_adjudication.md · Differentiation and the original-modulus average; Reduction to the single Mangoldt convolution
statement: The three differentiated reflected shifts give A(m)+log(k/m)(log*log)(m), with A=d_2*Lambda*Lambda*Lambda. The original-modulus unit average of e(−m/k) is mu(q)/phi(q), q=k/(k,m). The divisor products decay faster than any fixed power for the smooth cutoff; the remaining edge is (1/2) E_Cstar+O_N(T^−N), where Cstar=d_2*(Lambda log²).
hypotheses: Compact-local smooth contour formulation, k≤y≤T^theta, H=T^kappa with kappa>(1+theta)/2, bounded outer coefficients. Divisor removal is unconditional via Poisson or Hurwitz–Mellin cancellation. Arbitrary decay applies to discarded divisor pieces; inherited contour errors keep their separate bounds.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/uniform99_fixed_sequence_adjudication.md · Reduction to the single Mangoldt convolution
statement: The remaining sufficient target is Re E_Cstar=o(T log⁴T), with E_Cstar=∑_{k≤Y^(4b)} (c_k/k)∑_m Cstar(m) w_T(2πm/k)[e(−m/k)−mu(q)/phi(q)], q=k/(k,m), and c_k the coefficients of D⁴.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/release92_tightness_source_selection.md · Garsia and Rodemich; 1974 journal pp. 69–70, Theorem 1.2 and (1.2), (1.3), (1.7), (1.8)

statement: Petrov v1 Theorem 4.4, ordinary BOGC and finite Jacobi give det(U* A_n^−1 U)=(det Gamma/det Gamma(0)) L_obl/L_n for the rooted CUE cosine symbol. On the real Laplace axis both exact Gram and oblique tail determinants are strictly positive at every fixed N,z.
hypotheses: Fixed integers N≥2 and J≥1, analytic polynomial tilts X=T((1−w)^J) on N−1 free modes and exponential finite Laurent symbol. The source theorem requires its Gram to be invertible; real z gives the adjoint structure. The optional fixed-tail chart requires separate invertibility.

statement: The tilted tail contributes −kappa_(J,N) z² with kappa_(J,N)=Σ_(j<J)||H(F_+)*U_j||²>0. For N=4,J=2,k=2 the gap is 9/160; the optional chart determinant changes sign between z=0 and 8 while the exact factors remain positive.
hypotheses: Same fixed-rank cosine model. The ordinary ambient tail is stable in the stated coefficient window. For fixed 0<a<b≤1/2 the quadratic gap has the positive Riemann-sum limit in the note. The chart obstruction is separate from the zero of the extrapolated formal moment polynomial.
